activities.caption: what leaves vs what stays — drag the divider
activities.name: wcPurifierCompare

config.prompt: Evaporation sorts the ocean — drag between the two fractions:

before.label: What leaves — the vapour
before.text: Only the water molecules evaporate: pure H₂O lifts roughly 430,000 km³ into the air each year, an invisible gas.

after.label: What stays — the salts
after.text: The ocean keeps them: losing pure vapour for billions of years, it has grown steadily saltier — which is why rain is fresh even over the sea.

config.why: Evaporation is a purifier — the sorting that makes rain drinkable everywhere it falls.

activities.anchor: clouds form above the Amazon rainforest even in the dry season
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the plant-powered leg
activities.name: wcStomataCloze

config.text: Roots pull water from the soil and it escapes as vapour through leaf pores called %%0%% — a process named %%1%%. Add the two land losses together and water managers call the total %%2%%, because it measures exactly how much irrigation a crop region needs.
config.hint: The pores, the process, and the manager's portmanteau — the Amazon exhales its own clouds.

activities.anchor: the cargo: the whole atmosphere holds only about
activities.caption: call the atmosphere's instant stock
activities.name: wcAtmosEst

config.prompt: Emptying and refilling constantly — how much water is airborne worldwide at any given instant?
config.why: About 13,000 km³ — yet roughly 110,000 km³ lands on land surfaces every year, because the stock is emptied and refilled many times over.
config.context: A fast reservoir: the same division that makes rain end a crop drought within weeks.

activities.anchor: Then comes the decision that shapes everything downstream
activities.caption: where does each drop go? file the outcomes
activities.name: wcPathSort

items.label: sheeting over the surface into streams and rivers
the spring melt feeding rivers on schedule
soaking into soil and rock toward the water table
turning directly into vapour without melting first — sublimation

config.why: Every drop faces the same three-way decision — and which way it goes decides everything downstream, from flood timing to well yields.

activities.anchor: hurricanes are powered by exactly this release
activities.caption: bet before the reveal — the storm's engine
activities.name: wcHurricanePredict

config.q: A hurricane spins up over a warm ocean, then keeps running for days. What powers it once it is over water?
choices: The Sun's direct heating of the storm cloud tops
Condensation — the heat released each time vapour turns back into droplets
config.why: Evaporating water absorbs energy from its surroundings; condensing releases it again — a giant heat pump lifting energy from the tropical ocean and dropping it wherever the rain falls.

activities.anchor: You do not need special data to compute one
activities.caption: place the ocean's residence time
activities.name: wcOceanPlace

config.prompt: Stock divided by flux — place the ocean's residence time on the years scale.
config.why: About 3,100 years: 1.35 billion km³ losing roughly 430,000 km³ per year to evaporation — against the atmosphere's ~9 days, a clock on entirely different terms.

activities.name: wcBasinMatch

config.prompt: The return leg's plumbing — pair each term:

pairs.right: all precipitation drains toward one outlet
a stream funnelling into an ever larger one
volume of water passing a point per second — the one number that defines a river

config.why: The whole network behaves as one plumbing system — which is why geologists read stream maps like X-rays of the rocks beneath.

activities.anchor: Urbanisation replaces infiltrating soil with impermeable concrete
activities.caption: walk the flood-management decision
activities.name: wcFloodBranch

config.root: Your city floods, and the budget allows one big fix. Walk it.

choices.label: Raise the levees and channelise the river
choices.feedback: The banks rise and the water speeds onward — protected here, a bigger flood scheduled there.

choices.label: Zone the floodplain and restore wetlands — room for the river
choices.feedback: Costs land instead of certainty, and scales honestly — the Dutch adopted it after the 1995 floods.

downstream.text: Downstream towns now flood worse than before. What now?

choices.label: Build taller levees there too — keep passing the water on
choices.feedback: The invoice keeps moving down the valley — the mechanism the Great Mississippi Flood of 1993 wrote large.

choices.label: Give the river room upstream — remove the pinch point
choices.feedback: Working with the cycle: the floodplain was the landscape's designated overflow room all along.

done.text: Zoning, wetlands, room for the river: the fix that works with the basin instead of against it.

done2.text: Restored sponges and honest zoning — the flood still comes, but the landscape has somewhere to put it.

passon.text: Every raised bank schedules a larger flood for whoever lives below — and the river always has someone below.

config.why: A flood is the basin delivering more water than the channel can carry — engineering can move the invoice, not cancel it.
